To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

expert assessment of occupational exposures to lung cancer carcinogens showed fair to good reliability among teams of raters and high specificity for all agents, but poor sensitivity for 29 of 70 agents.
the agreement among teams of experts in the presence of an exposure was fair to good for the majority of the agents, and poor to fair for 29.

(1) the reliability of expert exposure assessment in the multicenter study of lung cancer was high for some agents, but low for others; (2) the sensitivity and specificity of expert assessment were high for all agents; (3) the reliability of the exposure assessment was not associated with the prevalence of exposure to the agent, but it was associated with the prevalence and the intensity of exposure; (4) the reliability was higher in jobs with a high prevalence and a high intensity of exposure; and
In summary, our research is concerned with
assessing the reliability of expert assessment of exposure to occupational agents in a case-control study of occupational lung cancer.
the assessment of exposure misclassification by expert assessment in multicenter occupational studies.
a methodological study of the reliability of expert assessment of occupational exposure in a multicenter study.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study show that expert assessment of occupational exposure can be a reliable method of exposure assessment in epidemiological studies, but the reliability depends on the exposure agent.
the reliability of the exposure assessment in this study was generally fair to good, with some agents having a higher reliability than others.
the reliability of expert exposure assessment is high, but that it is lower for some agents than for others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
expert assessment of exposure in a multicenter study can be expected to yield a fair to good level of reliability, but with considerable variability between agents.
the use of experts to assess exposure to occupational agents is a valid method for case-control studies.
, although expert assessment is a useful method for assessing exposure to a large number of agents in a large multicenter study, there is a considerable amount of misclassification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
expert assessment of occupational exposures is a valid approach for assessing the role of occupational agents in disease.
expert assessment of exposure is a feasible and valid method for occupational studies.
